business_scope.primary_industry_name: Public Commercial Web Scraping and Proxy API Gateways

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Common Law - codified statutes modeled principally on the U.S. Delaware General Corporation Law, supplemented by Marshallese customary law in land and title matters; judicial review by the RMI High Court and Supreme Court
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States (1986, as amended 2003)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) between RMI and the United States (signed 2006)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus, signed 14 June 2017)
No comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network; non-resident entities are taxed in RMI only on RMI-source income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC): Business Corporations Act (52 MIRC, as amended, modeled on Delaware General Corporation Law); Registered Agents Act 2004; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 ('AML/CFT Act 2018'), as amended; Criminal Code; FIU Regulations and Guidance Notes issued by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit ('FIU') pursuant to the AML/CFT Act 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Business Entities Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (filed via OAG-licensed Registered Agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - chain certification by the RMI Registrar and the RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, then legalization at the destination consulate; Hague Apostille is not available because RMI is not a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (verify HCCH status at issuance date)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation (post-filing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Business Entities Registry and the licensed Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the same chain; alternatively, for U.S.-based recipients, a Registrars-certified copy accompanied by notarization accepted under the recipients' internal customary practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Passport Copy and Proof of Residential Address of each Director, Officer, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public and competent authority in the document's origin country (e.g., U.S. state Notary and Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the originating country's competent authority (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State); RMI registered agents accept apostilled documents for standard KYC, or consular legalization where the origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Wealth Declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed attorney/accountant of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the origin state is an Apostille party) or notarized certified copy accepted under the Registered Agent's Customer Due Diligence procedures at the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all Directors, Officers, and UBOs against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List (UNSCR 1267/1989/2253); (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) UK OFSI Sanctions List; (v) RMI FIU published notices and domestic terrorist designation list; and (vi) adverse media and PEP databases with a 12-month post-employment PEP monitoring window. Screening is performed by the licensed Registered Agent at engagement, upon any register modification, and quarterly thereafter; a confirmed match triggers a Suspicious Activity Report filing with the RMI FIU within the statutory deadline.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Business Entities Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro - electronic name-clearance and reservation processed exclusively through OAG-licensed Registered Agents via the official RMI Registry e-Services system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English and Marshallese are official languages of the Republic; corporate names must be in Latin (Roman) script only. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered and reserved names and must end with a statutory suffix: 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or the abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.'. Marshallese-language names are permitted if romanized and accompanied by an English statutory suffix; financial-sector entities must additionally use the suffix mandated by their licensing statute.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Savings and Loan, Credit Union - prohibited without prior RMI banking license and Registrar consent
Trust, Trustee, Trust Company - prohibited without a license or written consent under the Registered Agents Act or Trust Acts
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance - prohibited without prior Insurance Commissioner approval
Co-operative, Building Society - prohibited without the relevant statutory license
Royal, Government, Commonwealth, State, Municipal, Authority, Agency - prohibited without official authorization or evidence of entitlement
University, College, Institute - sensitive, requires evidence of accreditation or ministerial consent
Chamber, Chamber of Commerce, Association - sensitive, requires entitlement evidence
Securities, Exchange, Digital Asset Exchange, Payday Lender, Money Services Business - requires prior regulatory authorization if the entity will conduct the regulated activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is renewable once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the renewal fee. Upon rejection, the applicant, through its Registered Agent, must file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 business days, stating the grounds of distinctiveness and attaching any required consent or license for sensitive tokens; the Registrar must determine the appeal within 10 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may resubmit a revised name immediately or, within 30 days of the final administrative decision, seek judicial review in the RMI High Court under the Civil Procedure Rules. In practice, a revised-name resubmission with expedited clearance is the most efficient remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible at this risk tier: every Marshall Islands Business Corporation must maintain a registered office at the office of its licensed Registered Agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands and a Registered Agent licensed under the Registered Agents Act 2004 for service of process. No physical office, local employees, or local directors are required, and the entity may be fully remotely operated. A 'virtual office' is therefore acceptable only as the Registered Agent's physical registered office, not as a mere mail-forwarding address. Third-party KYB by payment processors such as Stripe will require the agent certification of corporate existence and UBO documentation; this is a platform condition, not an RMI statutory requirement for ISIC 6201 activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 3% to 5% annual probability of unannounced FIU or Registrar inspection for a non-resident data-services Business Corporation with no local operations and no adverse alerts; upon a confirmed SAR trigger, adverse media, or APG/FATF mutual-evaluation scrutiny, inspection probability exceeds 50% and includes the Registered Agent's UBO records, CDD files, and on-site verification of the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Business Entities Registry, Office of the Attorney General (collected via licensed Registered Agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Registrar fee schedule; standard government tariff for name availability and reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Business Entities Registry, Office of the Attorney General
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory incorporation filing tariff for the standard authorized-share bracket (up to 25,000 shares)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office services (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI-licensed Registered Agent / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark annual retainer for non-resident Business Corporation administration and service of process

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC, UBO CDD file compilation, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent's compliance department (RMI AML/CFT Act 2018 obligations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed EDD fee for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier, including quarterly rescreening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille (where applicable), and consular legalization of director and UBO identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public, originating Secretary of State, destination consulate or RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary and apostille tariffs of the originating jurisdiction plus consular legalization and handling fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate records kit: minutes, share certificates, share register, UBO register, and corporate seal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Registered Agent / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for statutory records preparation and registered office file maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Courier delivery of original certificates and authenticated documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark international express rate from Majuro or issuing office to the client's jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal advisory review (AML/CFT structure, payment-processor KYB preparation, and name-clearance support)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External qualified attorney (RMI or U.S. corporate counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customary fixed-fee market benchmark for cross-border digital-business formation and compliance advisory

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, 1987, as amended (B.C.A.) - Part II (Incorporation), Part III (Registered Office and Registered Agent), Part V (Directors and Officers); supplemented by the Registered Agents Licensing Act and the Foreign Investment Business License Act where a physical presence is later established.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry Division, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (filings must be tendered through a locally licensed registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statutory form prescribed under the B.C.A.), executed by the incorporator and endorsed by the consent of the licensed resident registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorized capital for a non-resident business corporation; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration determined by the board (nominal US$1 acceptance is valid) and no escrow, deposit, or capital maintenance account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopt the Articles of Incorporation and accept the founding subscriber's subscription for 10,000 registered ordinary shares of no par value at US$1,000, declared fully paid.

RESOLVED, that the licensed registered agent's Majuro office be ratified as the Corporation's statutory registered office and agent.

RESOLVED, that the President, Secretary, and Treasurer named by the founding director be appointed as officers, with authority to open bank accounts and execute contracts, and to file the non-resident tax-exempt status documentation.

RESOLVED, that share certificates be issued and all annual registry filings be caused by the officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed resident registered agent (online gateway) with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three (3) ranked corporate name choices in English. The Registrar rejects names that are confusingly similar to an existing entity or that imply banking, insurance, trust, or government sponsorship without authorization. Obtain written name clearance before drafting the Articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and suffix (Corporation, Inc., Limited)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-tender a fresh name list; if a name is queried for confusion, file a letter of explanation with consent of the existing holder or proceed with the second-ranked name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator before a notary public (or a licensed registered agent attesting execution under the B.C.A.).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in statutory form: corporate name, registered agent and registered office address in Majuro, authorized capital (e.g., 10,000 no-par shares), statement of non-resident domestic corporation status, and incorporator name and address. Execute before a notary and obtain the registered agent's signed consent.
required_dossiers: Proof of principal place of business outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands (utility bill or lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar notes drafting defects in capital clauses or the non-resident designation, restate the Articles by amendment and re-submit with a corrected signature block.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (electronic submission through the licensed agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles through the Registrar's e-submission channel together with the state filing fee of US$150 and the statement of non-resident status. Obtain an electronic filing acknowledgment and a date-stamped fee receipt.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Filing checklist endorsed by the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct defects within 14 days by letter of explanation; if the Registrar refuses, withdraw and re-file corrected Articles or pursue appellate review by the Registrar within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a certified copy of the filed Articles. The agent retrieves both, verifies the corporate details, and records the incorporation date in the corporate register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains ministerial errors, file a Certificate of Correction with the Registrar, obtain a reissued Certificate, and replace the defective document in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Resolutions, Share Subscription, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding director and incorporator (unanimous written consents valid under the B.C.A.).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting or execute unanimous written consents: approve the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, adopt bylaws, approve the share issuance, elect directors and officers, and open the minute book, share ledger, and corporate seal records.
required_dossiers: Written consent in lieu of first meeting
Officer appointment forms and acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective officer appointment or share issuance is cured by a subsequent unanimous written consent ratifying all action taken in the Corporation's name and confirming the share register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Tax Status Confirmation and Annual Maintenance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations and licensed registered agent (tax registry notification to the Ministry of Finance).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the Corporation's non-resident domestic status so that income derived outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands remains outside the RMI income tax base; calendar the annual registry fee and confirmation statement due on the anniversary of incorporation; file the annual statement with the Registrar to retain good standing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual confirmation is flagged, file a late reinstatement application with the Registrar, pay arrears and penalty, and obtain a Certificate of Good Standing restoring full status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 data-processing, commercial scraping, and proxy API gateway services are non-industrial and do not trigger any manufacturing or extractive licensing regime in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the non-resident entity in its offshore capacity; if a physical RMI presence is later established, the contingent licenses are: (i) Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) under the Foreign Investment Business License Act issued by the Foreign Investment Board; and (ii) municipal Business License under the Business License Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 3 (no physical installation); the activity is a pure digital data and API commerce gateway with no construction, manufacturing, discharge, or land disturbance, so no EIA study is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the offshore digital service; contingent thresholds if server-adjacent offices are opened in RMI: no untreated wastewater discharge (compliance with municipal sewer BOD/COD limits), VOC emissions below EPA site thresholds, and e-waste disposal only through EPA-approved certified recyclers under RMI waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the pure offshore entity; contingent onsite requirements where physical infrastructure is hosted: RMI Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (civil defense clearance), structural load certification for rack equipment, and occupational health clearance under RMI OHS standards for any staff presence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Tax and Revenue Office, Majuro Atoll; no dedicated public taxpayer portal exists, and filings are effected through the Tax and Revenue Office and national treasury.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is issued to non-resident business corporations because the RMI imposes no corporate income tax, VAT, GST, or general sales tax. The operative registration identifier is the Certificate of Incorporation and registration number issued by the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act. Where local payroll occurs, the entity obtains an employer contribution number from the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration; no general tax file number is otherwise procurable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable: no check-the-box election or OECD-style hybrid mismatch election exists in the RMI. A foreign-owned limited company may elect to be treated as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation under the Business Corporations Act by filing a non-resident domestic corporation statement, which confirms exemption from national income tax and confirms treatment as not carrying on trade or business in the RMI for tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not applicable: the RMI does not impose VAT, GST, or a general sales and use tax; indirect taxation is limited to customs import duty and municipal business license or gross revenue charges for local activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold exists because no VAT or GST system is in force. Importers must present declarations to RMI Customs for inward duty assessment; exporters have no separate indirect tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None: RMI law imposes no real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API integration, or digital stamping obligation. Customs declarations are lodged through the national customs administration, and no taxpayer-facing clearance API mandate applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable: absent VAT or GST, there is no export zero-rating mechanism and no indirect tax refund arises. Exports from the RMI are outside the customs import duty base. Where banking or contractual documentation requires proof of export proceeds, a 180-day repatriation documentary benchmark is commonly observed, but the RMI imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward remittance certificate or bank statement showing offshore payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating clawback is possible because no VAT exists. False customs declarations may attract customs fines, forfeiture of goods, and prosecution under RMI customs legislation. Misrepresenting non-resident domestic corporation status before the Registrar may result in loss of the tax-exempt classification, reinstatement of assessed national tax liability where applicable, and monetary penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Ministry of Finance); the Marshall Islands has no domestic central bank, and U.S. Federal Reserve monetary policy governs USD-denominated liquidity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the sole official currency and legal tender. There is no exchange-control law, no capital-account restriction, and no current-account restriction imposed by the RMI Government. Capital contributions, dividends, interest, service fees, and liquidation proceeds may be freely remitted in USD or any permitted foreign currency. The practical constraints arise only at the bank and correspondent-bank level through AML/KYC screening, OFAC sanctions filters, and source-of-funds verification. A non-resident business corporation is not subject to profit-remittance permits or prior approval from the Banking Commissioner.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement exists in the Marshall Islands. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no timeline requiring export/earnings receipts to be repatriated into USD or deposited with a local bank. A non-resident BC may hold export proceeds in USD or foreign currencies at its treasury discretion, subject to the account terms of its licensed commercial bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Multi-Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam — Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Risk but structurally constrained. The Marshall Islands does not issue dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licences, and offshore digital EMIs cannot hold themselves out as regulated RMI payment service providers. Stripe is not locally licensed and does not maintain a direct acquiring presence in the RMI; it may be available only indirectly through a third-country partner merchant processor, which creates settlement and onboarding uncertainty. The more viable fintech rail is USDC-based treasury routing via licensed crypto-currency custodians/off-ramps such as Coinbase or Circle, combined with a traditional USD bank account for fiat settlement. The use of unlicensed EMIs to serve RMI residents would be unlawful, but an offshore EMI account held outside the RMI for cross-border vendor and API-revenue flows is permissible as a treasury tool.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring directors of a Marshall Islands non-resident business corporation to appear physically before a bank. Licensed local banks will normally accept a remote/electronic KYC package supported by independent e-KYC verification, notarised corporate documents, and a board resolution authorising account opening. In practice, the Bank of Marshall Islands and the Bank of Guam RMI Branch may request a video conference interview or a notarised meeting attendance packet, especially for non-resident directors and beneficial owners. U.S. correspondent banks may impose an additional in-person or authorised-representative interview before clearing wires, but this is a bank policy rather than a government mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors residing in jurisdictions not recognised by the bank's internal risk-scoring model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, proof of residential address dated within three months, professional reference letter from a regulated lawyer/accountant, curriculum vitae showing legitimate business history, and a detailed source-of-wealth statement with supporting bank statements or investment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Issuance or possibility of bearer share certificates, which are treated as a high AML risk by correspondent banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of no bearer shares issued by the RMI registered agent, certified register of members and directors, beneficial ownership declaration under the RMI Business Corporations Act, and an irrevocable undertaking to maintain only registered shares on the accounts of the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope as a public commercial web-scraping and proxy API gateway, which may be perceived as facilitating anonymous traffic or data resale with weak counterparty due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts with data consumers, defined acceptable-use policy, IP-address and user-agent logging procedures, customer identity verification workflow, privacy policy and data-pipeline audit trail, and a written AML/transaction-monitoring manual that flags unusual API-service receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection funded through cryptocurrency or USDC, raising source-of-funds ambiguities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain analytics report from a recognised forensics vendor, real-time conversion trail from USDC/Crypto to fiat USD through a licensed exchange, exchange invoices, wallet ownership attestation, and a sworn source-of-funds affidavit supported by prior transaction records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing starts with a fiat USD transfer from the beneficial owner's regulated bank account via SWIFT MT103, normally using the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) network and either Fedwire or CHIPS for the U.S. dollar leg. The remittance purpose field should be explicit and consistent with the entity's opening file: 'Capital Contribution' or 'Subscription for Shares of MH_BC'. Beneficiary identification must match the RMI BC legal name and account number at the receiving bank. There is no FX conversion requirement because the RMI uses USD domestically, so the injected funds are maintained directly as USD. For USDC or crypto-denominated injections, the funds must first be off-ramped to fiat through a licensed crypto custodian, documented with a source-of-funds report, and then transmitted through a standard MT103/Fedwire to the RMI bank account; direct USDC-to-bank settlement is not currently supported by RMI commercial banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The standard clearing rails for trade settlements are SWIFT MT103 for vendor and API-supplier payments, SWIFT MT202 for interbank transfers, and commercial documentary letters of credit (LC) for high-value or risk-mitigated procurement of data infrastructure, bandwidth, or proxy services. Because the target business scope involves data pipeline and web-scraping API services, the predominant payment pattern will be recurring MT103 payments to overseas technology vendors and cloud providers. USDC can be used for vendors that accept stablecoin, via Coinbase/Circle wallet-to-wallet transfer, but only after an OFAC comparison and beneficiary verification. For commercial LC transactions, the RMI BC's account bank will issue or confirm the LC through a corresponding U.S. or Asian gateway bank, and the seller's presenting bank will receive settlement under normal UCP 600 rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-currency forward contracts (USD vs EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD) with licensed counterparty banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term USD-denominated treasury positions
Vanilla European-style currency options for downside protection on non-USD operational expenditures
FX spot contracts for treasury conversions; no non-deliverable forward (NDF) market is needed because the RMI operates solely on USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Corporate License Fee Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 November of each calendar year, irrespective of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100 after 30 November; continued delinquency beyond one year results in administrative strike-off, loss of legal capacity to transact business, and restoration only upon payment of all arrears and penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement under the Business Corporations Act for a non-resident Business Corporation; an independent audit is required only if the corporation is licensed under the Marshall Islands Banking Act, Insurance Act, or Trust Companies Act, is listed on a recognized stock exchange, or receives a binding shareholder direction to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No local GAAP is separately promulgated for non-resident Business Corporations; financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or US GAAP as elected by the board of directors, and books of account must be maintained at the registered office or principal place of business.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public UBO register or annual UBO filing exists in the Marshall Islands; shareholding and transfer information is maintained confidentially in the Register of Members. The annual report merely confirms total authorized and issued share capital and director details; any transfer of shares is recorded in the Register of Members and no separate annual confirmation filing is required.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – 850 per annum for registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 6,000 for a certified audit if voluntarily or externally required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective for a non-resident tax-exempt Business Corporation (RMI tax-exemption zone); the onshore statutory Gross Revenue Tax for taxation-zone entities is 3% of gross revenue.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident domestic BC qualifies for the permanent RMI tax-exemption zone regime: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no gross revenue tax on foreign-source income. Only fixed annual franchise/registration fees apply (e.g., USD 200 per year for a standard 50,000-share authorization, scaled by authorized share capital).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Report and Registration Renewal under the RMI Business Corporations Act, submitted electronically through the RMI Registrar of Corporations e-filing portal or by the appointed RMI-licensed registered agent. No corporate income tax return form exists for non-resident tax-exempt BCs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (anniversary-date cycle; no fiscal-year income tax return is required for non-resident BCs)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due each year on the incorporation anniversary date (Annual Report Date); filings are accepted within a short administrative grace window before penalties accrue. The deadline is service-act anniversary-driven rather than a fiscal-year-end tax deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Name and File Serial Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered corporate name and the RMI file/serial number as stated in the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name exactly as registered with the statutory corporate ending (e.g., Corporation, Inc., Ltd., or Company); the file number is found on the Application for Registration and must match all prior filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Agent and Registered Office Address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical street address in the Marshall Islands of the licensed registered agent maintaining the BC's corporate records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC may not act as its own registered agent; retain a Majuro-based licensed trust or registered-agent firm. A post office box is insufficient for the registered office address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total number of authorized shares, class structure, par value or stated capital without par value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the same capital structure shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; this declaration is the basis for computing the annual franchise tax fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A two-to-three sentence description of the actual commercial business conducted by the BC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the business as public commercial web-scraping, data feeds and proxy API gateway subscriptions, referencing ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210; confirm no RMI-source revenue, no RMI employees, and no RMI premises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attestation that the BC is non-resident and derives income exclusively from sources outside the RMI taxation zone.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a documented support file proving the absence of RMI-source receipts: customer invoices from the data gateway, foreign operating bank and Stripe settlement statements, and USDC treasury wallet records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the anniversary date incurs a late fee of 10% of the annual franchise tax/fees; prolonged default leads to administrative dissolution by the RMI Registrar, revocation of the certificate of good standing, and loss of the BC's separate legal personality in foreign court proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Return (ESR) filed with the RMI Registrar under the Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2023 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2023, via the Registrar's online compliance portal; applicable to financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2024.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months of the end of the BC's financial year; an initial relevant-activity notification is due at registration or annual renewal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the BC carries on a relevant activity as defined by the Economic Substance Regulations (e.g., Distribution and Service Centres, Headquarters, Leasing, Financing, Shipping, or Pure IP Holding).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify the proxy-API and web-scraping data gateway as a Distribution and Service Centre if revenue is derived from reselling access to data-gathering services; otherwise declare non-relevancy with a factual supporting note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box ESR-B - Foreign Tax Residence Election or Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the foreign jurisdiction of tax residence and the foreign tax reference or company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A valid election removes RMI ESR substance obligations if the BC is actually tax-resident in a foreign jurisdiction imposing income tax; an unsupported or sham election is itself a compliance violation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counts of management and board meetings held in the RMI, RMI-based employees, RMI physical premises, and local expenditure amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the BC is RMI-resident for ESR purposes, provide genuine evidence: minutes of director meetings conducted in Majuro, RMI employment agreements, a leased service office, and RMI payroll records proportionate to income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box ESR-D - Income and Expenditure Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income, expenditure, and operating expenses attributable to the relevant activity for the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the API gateway's Stripe settlement reports and USDC on-chain flows with the substance metrics; unexplained revenue booked without corresponding RMI substance is the primary audit trigger.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fixed civil penalty of USD 10,000 for non-filing; daily default penalty of USD 1,000 per day of continuing contravention; deliberate false statements carry penalties up to USD 50,000 and risk deregistration of the BC.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by a non-resident Business Corporation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable - the RMI maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreements or treaty relief/TRC administrative network. Repatriation protocol: approve the dividend by board resolution under the BCA solvency test; record the distribution in corporate minutes; effect payment through the operating bank account or USDC treasury wallet; foreign shareholders bear no RMI withholding tax but must verify taxability under their own residence-state laws.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest: 0%. Treaty-reduced rates are not available because the RMI has no DTA network. The primary risk is foreign-side withholding tax in the counterparty's jurisdiction and the RMI ESR prohibition on 'pure IP holding' activities without genuine substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 - no statutory transfer-pricing documentation or Local File/Master File regime exists under RMI law for non-resident BCs. The de facto threshold is the RMI good-standing and prudence standard: maintain contemporaneous contracts, pricing schedules, and substance/AML records interoperable with ESR filings and banking KYC reviews.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations create a substance-over-revenue doctrine for RMI-registered entities carrying on relevant activities from FY 2024. A web-scraping/proxy API gateway classified as a Distribution and Service Centre must demonstrate RMI management and control, adequate RMI employees and premises, and income proportionality unless it validly declares foreign tax residence. Failure converts the nominally tax-exempt BC into a reportable shell and exposes the corporate veil to piercing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving RMI-source gross revenue (e.g., physical server infrastructure in Majuro, direct subscription sales to RMI customers, or an independent agent habitually concluding contracts in the RMI) while the BC files the annual declaration and ESR claiming strict non-resident tax-exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the BC into the RMI taxation zone: assessment of the 3% Gross Revenue Tax with interest; penalty up to 50% of the assessed tax; the Registrar may strike the BC from the corporate register; the entity loses good standing and access to the RMI courts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for restitution of assessed tax, penalties, and costs; fraudulent misrepresentation supports criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years and veil-piercing so shareholders and directors face direct personal enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an empty vessel: no ESR filing, no RMI office, no resident director meetings, while using the BC as a pass-through for subscription data and API fees converted from Stripe fiat into USDC, thereby misrepresenting tax-exempt status to customers and banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR fixed penalty of USD 10,000; daily default penalty of USD 1,000; escalating penalty up to USD 50,000 for deliberate misrepresentation; publication on the Registrar's non-compliance list and consequent debanking of the BC's banking and correspondent accounts; ultimate deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and the registered agent are individually liable for penalties where defaults result from their directions; the Registrar may disqualify them from future directorships, impose travel bans as enforcement security, and pierce the shell so personal assets respond for RMI registry fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing scraped personal or payment-card data without lawful basis, onboarding sanctioned or high-risk users, and deliberately structuring receipts across Stripe and USDC rails to obscure the economic origin of data-pipeline fees through multiple proxy wallets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the RMI Money Laundering Control Act and AML/CFT Regulations: criminal fines up to USD 1,000,000 or twice the value laundered, and imprisonment up to 10 years; the financial regulator or Registrar may freeze Stripe settlement balances and USDC addresses, cancel the BC's registration, and place the entity and its principals on financial-action lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or benefit from the layering scheme face criminal money-laundering liability, civil confiscation, red-notice/passport-level travel bans, extradition exposure to counterparty jurisdictions, and veil-piercing as the corporation is merely an instrumentality of the principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing 100% of operating cash (Stripe settlement funds and USDC balances) to shareholders as dividends immediately before supplier liabilities or customer refunds mature, leaving the BC without capital while continuing to claim limited liability in subscription and API contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI fraudulent-conveyance principles: avoidance and clawback of the transfers and reinstatement of creditor claims against the entity; directors breach fiduciary duty under the Business Corporations Act and are liable for unlawful distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution orders against directors; individual liability requiring board members to repay the value of unlawful distributions; in aggravated cases courts order veil-piercing and attach shareholder conduct, permitting worldwide asset enforcement.
